subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological quantum materials
motivation: The quantum Hall effect required strong magnetic fields. Haldane showed in 1988 that quantized Hall conductance could in principle arise from band topology alone, but for 25 years no real material did it. In 2010 Rui Yu, Zhong Fang, Xi Dai and colleagues predicted that magnetically doped Bi2Se3-family thin films would show a quantum anomalous Hall state. In 2013 Qi-Kun Xue's team observed it in Cr-doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 films grown by MBE. This needed atomic-level control of film growth, doping, thickness and Fermi level. The result was a quantized Hall plateau h/e² at zero field, carried by dissipationless chiral edge states. It is a true '0 to 1' discovery in which theory and materials growth worked together. It has been reproduced worldwide and later extended to MnBi2Te4 and moiré systems. It has opened the field of intrinsic magnetic topological matter, with prospects for low-power electronics and topological quantum devices.
